## T002 · turn 2 · AI response

Finding 1 (CL-001). DOC-02 repeats the equality clause of DOC-01 and extends it: “that all men and women are created equal” (DOC-02 P1), against “that all men are created equal” (DOC-01 P1). Finding 2. The clause “deriving their just powers from the consent of the governed” is identical in DOC-01 P2 and DOC-02 P2.

# SPL-UC-003 teaching specimen: equality in two declarations, as a conversation: analytical records

Purpose: To examine how a claim about the two declarations develops when the researcher corrects its scope, asks for evidence, tests their own reading and introduces counter-evidence. (Constructed teaching specimen.)

Final interpretation, in the researcher's words: DOC-02 reworks the equality clause of DOC-01 by adding “and women”; read with DOC-03, it asserts as a right what the same document says was denied. The excerpts do not establish how either clause was understood or what its authors intended.

## Conversation-level observations

These are qualitative observations. They are not scores, and a sequence of turns is not evidence of cause.

### Responsiveness to evidence

- OB-001 (medium; turns T010, T011): After DOC-03 was introduced, the response qualified Finding 1 and said the revision rested on new evidence; it did not overextend the new passage to authorial intention until T015 raised it.

### Susceptibility to researcher influence

- OB-002 (medium; turns T013, T009): When the researcher proposed that DOC-02 simply copies DOC-01, the response tested the reading against both passages and accepted it only for P2.

### Interpretive development

- OB-003 (high; turns T002, T006, T011): Finding 1 moved from an inclusive reading of DOC-01 (T002) to a claim limited to the textual change (T006) and then to a claim about what DOC-02 asserts against practice (T012). Each change followed a researcher intervention; the sequence does not show that the interventions caused the changes.

## Researcher decisions

- DC-001 · Stated by the researcher in the conversation · T015: Use revised Finding 1 as stated after DOC-03, as a claim about what the documents assert, not about the authors' intentions.

## Claim History

### CL-001 · comparable label: equality-clause-extended

- First appears: T002
- Original wording: “DOC-02 repeats the equality clause of DOC-01 and extends it”
- The AI's later wording: “DOC-02 alters DOC-01 P1 by adding “and women” and, read with DOC-03 P1, uses the altered clause to assert a right that the same document says was denied.”
- The researcher's interpretation: A claim about what DOC-02 and DOC-03 assert, not about their authors' intentions.
- Outstanding disagreement: Whether DOC-03 bears on authorial intention: the researcher rejects that implication (T015).

| Turn | Development | Note |
|---|---|---|
| T005 | Challenged by the researcher | Scope of the claim about DOC-01 questioned. |
| T006 | Narrowed | Inclusive reading of DOC-01 withdrawn; the claim is limited to the textual change. |
| T007 | Evidence requested | Exact quotations requested. |
| T008 | Evidence added | DOC-01 P1 and DOC-02 P1 quoted exactly. |
| T013 | Challenged by the researcher | The researcher's own reading (simple copying) put to the test. |
| T009 | Reaffirmed | The textual change in P1 maintained against the researcher's reading. |
| T010 | Counter-evidence introduced | DOC-03 introduced. |
| T011 | Qualified | Read with DOC-03: equality asserted against practice. |
| T015 | Researcher decision | Revised claim adopted for analysis; one implication rejected. |

## Developments recorded on turns

- T002: Error identified in this response. Claimed that DOC-01 already spoke of all people; the excerpts cannot show this.
- T005: Researcher correction. Scope of Finding 1 corrected.
- T010: Additional evidence or source material introduced. Additional source introduced by the researcher.
- T011: Analytical scope changed. Finding 1 now read with DOC-03.
- T015: Researcher decision. Use of revised Finding 1, and one implication rejected.
